body: claimed: M5 (issue-worker-high) · 2026-11-12T01:10Z · branch issue/982-lift-acceptance-tolerance · plan: compare the microlifted plan to the spiral within a stated tolerance instead of on equal half-degree steps; pin the slot's plan under 16 nm–0.25 um perturbations

unclaim: M5 worker (issue-worker-high) releases #982 without a PR and **escalates it to `effort:max`**. I cannot set labels from the fork, so a maintainer please swap `effort:high` for `effort:max` and drop `claimed`.

**Held work:** branch `issue/982-lift-acceptance-tolerance` on mkinney/Camcraft, commit 39a06802 (cut from upstream/main f490458a). No PR. The decision record is `docs/decisions/982-lift-acceptance-tolerance.md` on that branch.

**The premise is partly wrong: this is not measurement noise.** Readings are counts of rim samples (360 over 180 deg), so there is no unquantized reading to compare. On the slot the bound is 47.5014 deg. Swept in release with the opening eroded 0/16/32/62/125/250/510 nm deeper than it dilates back (a `cfg(test)` knob, `rings::OPEN_INSET`), the spiral read 47.5 every time, and the lifted plan read 47.5 every time except at 32 nm, where it read 48.0 (15.71 % D against the 15.38 % bound). That is one real sample over the bound, not a tie.

**Where the 48.0 comes from:** a growth piece cut in spiral order (every piece it depends on already cut), reached by a lifted return. Riding the spiral's own air onto it changes nothing. With `coarsen` switched off, no over-bound reading appears at any inset. So each coarse chord piece (`thin_turn`, 0.01 mm sag, 4 deg) reads within the bound itself but leaves a sliver that a later piece then cuts.

**Tried, both fail the Done-means:**
1. **One-sample tolerance** (`lifted <= max(spiral, bound) + 0.5 deg`, never over the cap). It keeps the slot, but it posts a plan that reads over the stated bound. On main it also flips `rotary_adaptive::the_r62_neck_levels_are_refused_for_travel_by_name` (radius 5.7 posted at 48.0 against 47.5). Dropped as a Prime Directive breach.
2. **Fine-chord retry** (held commit): keep the strict law, and when the lifted plan fails on its worst reading, rebuild it once with no coarsening. The slot keeps its lifted plan at 16 nm, 32 nm and 0.25 um. motion lib (191 + pin), `adaptive_hsm` 6/6 and `adaptive_band` 2/2 keep their verdicts (release, `--include-ignored`). It also rescues the r6.2 neck levels 5.7 and 5.2, which read 47.5 on the planner's own stock. On the dexel stock both read **20.3 % D** (the suite's law is <= 19.8 %), and radius 5.2 has **3 in-cut breaks past 5 deg**. The rewritten pin `the_r62_neck_levels_are_hsm_planned_under_the_load_and_kink_laws` is red on that.

**Why it is effort:max:** any acceptance-level rule that keeps the slot at 32 nm without an overload also rescues those rotary bands, whose plans the dexel measure rejects. Landing it needs one of these: `coarsen` repaired so it never leaves a sliver for the next piece (a planner algorithm change, and it would rescue the same rotary levels), or the r6.2 bands keeping a refusal of their own (#44/#47 thin-band work), or the planner/dexel load disagreement on developed bands fixed.

**#882's held fix on top of this:** trial-merged 70ac996f onto 39a06802. The slot's lib tests pass (lifted plan, no overload note), but `adaptive_hsm::hsm_report_full_resolution` still measures the slot at **73.7 % D**, with 44 in-cut breaks (worst 51.4 deg), 1 RapidInStock and 4 descents for 2 levels. That is the same as #882's "0.25 um + inset" row, so #882 is not unblocked by this.

claim by @mkinney withdrawn (unclaim comment) - issue is free again. Escalation applied as requested: `effort:high` -> `effort:max` (worker found the work bigger than the label; one real sample over the bound, not a tie - findings above). Held work: branch issue/982-lift-acceptance-tolerance @ 39a06802 (mkinney/Camcraft, cut from f490458a), decision record docs/decisions/982-lift-acceptance-tolerance.md on that branch.

fix on issue/982-microlift-acceptance · PR #1080 · pinned by adaptive::tests::the_slot_and_its_32_nm_twin_decide_the_same_way, adaptive::lift_tests::a_piece_takes_longer_chords_only_where_they_leave_no_sliver, adaptive::lift_tests::the_lifted_plan_is_kept_only_at_or_under_the_spiral_reading, adaptive::tests::the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations (heavy), rotary_adaptive::the_r62_neck_levels_are_hsm_planned_on_microlift_returns (heavy) · merges when reviewed

What it does: no tolerance was added. The 48.0 against 47.5 was one real rim sample, from the sliver a piece's longer chords leave for the next piece; a piece now takes longer chords only where they leave no cell standing that its own chords clear, and the acceptance stays strict. 30 of 30 slot twins (openings 8 nm - 1 um deeper, the slot 250 nm narrower to 5 um wider) keep the lifted plan; before, 10 of 30 dropped it.

One Done-means line is not met, on purpose: the rotary r6.2 neck levels' verdict changes (refused for travel -> HSM-planned on microlift returns). That verdict was this same coin on main (one level or the other is HSM-planned with the openings 16, 62, 250 or 510 nm deeper), and nothing at plan time tells those bands from the slot. Their pin is rewritten; their readings that stand past the whole bar's laws (20.3 % D at the bore exit, three 5.1-5.5 deg breaks on 5.2) are #1050. The #850 budget knife edge on the other rotary levels is #1051. Stacked on PR #1007. Decision record: docs/decisions/982-microlift-acceptance.md on the branch.
